Build a reference network

Source: R/reference-network.R
reference_network.Rd

reference_network() builds a co-citation or equivalence network among cited references. In a co-citation network two references are linked when they are cited together by the same paper; the equivalence network instead uses the cosine similarity of the references' citing-paper vectors.

Usage

reference_network(
  data,
  type = "co_citation",
  counting = "full",
  similarity = "none",
  threshold = 0,
  min_occur = 1L,
  top_n = NULL,
  self_loops = FALSE,
  deduplicate = TRUE,
  format = "edgelist",
  references = "references",
  sep = ";",
  strip_quotes = TRUE,
  id = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per work and a references column (list-column or delimited string). An id column is optional (see id).

type

Character. "co_citation" (default) or "equivalence" (cosine similarity of the references' citing-paper vectors; counting and similarity are ignored).

counting

Character. Counting method: "full" (default), "fractional", "paper" or "strength".

similarity

Character. Similarity measure. Default "none".

threshold

Numeric. Minimum edge weight; edges with weight < threshold are dropped. Default 0 (keep all).

min_occur

Integer. Minimum times a reference must be cited. Default 1.

top_n

Integer or NULL. Keep only the top_n most frequent nodes and return the edges among them. Default NULL (all nodes).

self_loops

Logical. If TRUE, include self-loops (an entity linked to itself). Default FALSE. Only takes effect with similarity = "none"; every similarity measure zeroes the diagonal.

deduplicate

Logical. If TRUE (default), each (paper, entity) pair is counted at most once – duplicate entries in the source data (e.g., the same author listed twice on a paper) are treated as one occurrence. Set to FALSE to count every raw occurrence.

format

Character. Output format:

"edgelist"

Default. A bibnets_network data frame with columns from, to, weight, count.

"gephi"

Gephi-ready data frame: Source, Target, Weight, Count, Type.

"igraph"

An igraph graph object (requires igraph).

"cograph"

A cograph_network object (requires cograph).

"matrix"

A sparse adjacency matrix.

references

Character. Name of the column containing cited references. Default "references".

sep

Character. Separator used to split the references column when it is a plain character column. Default ";". Ignored for list-columns.

strip_quotes

Logical. If TRUE (default), surrounding quote characters are removed from each reference.

id

Optional. Name of the column to use as the work identifier (the matrix-row dimension). If NULL (default), an existing id column is used when present, otherwise row numbers are used.

Value

Depends on format. The default "edgelist" returns a bibnets_network data frame with one row per undirected edge, columns from, to, weight and count, sorted by decreasing weight, and attributes network_type, counting and similarity. See author_network() for the other formats.

Details

The citing papers and their references form a two-mode matrix that is projected onto the references; counting and similarity weight the edges and threshold, min_occur and top_n prune them. It returns a bibnets_network edge list by default. To link the citing documents instead (bibliographic coupling or direct citation), use document_network().

Examples

data(biblio_data)
reference_network(biblio_data)
#> # bibnets network: reference_co_citation | 13 nodes · 38 edges | counting: full 
#>     from  to  weight  count
#>  1  R3    W1       4      4
#>  2  R1    R2       3      3
#>  3  R2    R5       3      3
#>  4  R2    W1       3      3
#>  5  R4    W1       3      3
#>  6  R3    W2       3      3
#>  7  W1    W2       3      3
#>  8  R2    R3       2      2
#>  9  R3    R4       2      2
#> 10  R1    R5       2      2
#> # ... 28 more edges
reference_network(biblio_data, similarity = "association")
#> # bibnets network: reference_co_citation | 13 nodes · 38 edges | counting: full | similarity: association 
#>     from  to  weight  count
#>  1  R9    W5       1      1
#>  2  R7    R9     0.5      1
#>  3  R7    W5     0.5      1
#>  4  R10   R6    0.25      1
#>  5  R6    W2    0.25      2
#>  6  R10   W3    0.25      1
#>  7  R6    W3    0.25      1
#>  8  R7    W3    0.25      1
#>  9  R1    R5  0.2222      2
#> 10  R1    R2     0.2      3
#> # ... 28 more edges
